input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages—those MMS things—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

I just checked, and it looks like I can't send picture messages (MMS) at all right now. Also, I’m not sure if my mobile data is working, and I don’t think I’m connected to Wi-Fi either. What should I do next?
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars, mobile data, or Wi-Fi icons. What does that mean?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now, I see a "no signal" icon and something about data being disabled. I still don’t see any signal bars or Wi-Fi icons. What should I do next?
I checked, and my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. What does that mean? Is that why I can’t send picture messages?

Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in. Now my phone shows one bar for signal and says "2G," but it still says data is disabled. I haven’t tried sending a picture message yet. What should I do next?

I turned on mobile data, but my phone still says "2G" and only shows one bar for signal. I checked, and it looks like my phone is set to use only 2G. How do I change it to 4G or something better? I’m not sure where to find that setting.

I changed the network mode like you said, and now my phone shows excellent signal and says "5G" with data enabled. But I still can’t send picture messages—it's still not working. Is there something else I should try? This is getting a bit frustrating.

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." I’m not sure if that’s right or not. Should I still try resetting these settings, or is there something else I should do?
I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else I can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I ever be able to send photos again?
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else I can try? I’m really starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all this.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages—those MMS things—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you with your MMS issue.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you, John. I’ve identified your account. To help you fix the MMS issue, I’ll need you to perform a few checks on your phone. 

First, could you please check if you can send regular text messages (SMS) and if your mobile data is working for other apps (like browsing the web)? This will help determine if the issue is specific to MMS or related to your overall service or data connection.

Let me know the results, and I’ll guide you through the next steps.

I just checked, and it looks like I can't send picture messages (MMS) at all right now. Also, I’m not sure if my mobile data is working, and I don’t think I’m connected to Wi-Fi either. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. Since you’re unsure about your mobile data and Wi-Fi connection, let’s start by confirming your phone’s current network and data status.

Please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any signal bars (and how many),
- If you see “LTE,” “4G,” “5G,” or similar,
- If there’s an airplane icon,
- If you see a mobile data icon or Wi-Fi icon.

If you’re not sure how to check, let me know, and I can guide you through the steps. This information will help me determine the next troubleshooting steps for your MMS issue.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars, mobile data, or Wi-Fi icons. What does that mean?

Thank you for the details. The airplane icon means your phone is in Airplane Mode, which disables all wireless connections—including cellular service, mobile data, and Wi-Fi. That’s why you can’t send MMS or use mobile data.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
- Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings panel,
- Tapping the airplane icon to turn it off.

Once you’ve turned off Airplane Mode, check if your signal bars and mobile data icons reappear. Let me know when you’ve done this, and if you can now send picture messages or see your signal return. If not, I’ll guide you through the next steps.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: missing
Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none
Mobile Data Enabled: No
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now, I see a "no signal" icon and something about data being disabled. I still don’t see any signal bars or Wi-Fi icons. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since you now see a "no signal" icon and data is disabled, let's check if your SIM card is being recognized by your phone. This will help us determine if the issue is with your SIM card or network connection.

Please check your phone’s SIM card status. If you need instructions, let me know your phone model, and I can guide you. Once you check, let me know if your phone says the SIM is active, missing, or locked.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
I checked, and my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. What does that mean? Is that why I can’t send picture messages?

Yes, if your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, that is the reason you can’t send picture messages (MMS) or use mobile data. The SIM card is required for your phone to connect to the cellular network.

Let’s try to fix this by reseating your SIM card. Please follow these steps:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Remove the SIM card tray and take out the SIM card.
3. Carefully reinsert the SIM card, making sure it’s properly aligned.
4. Put the tray back in and power your phone back on.

After your phone restarts, check if it now detects the SIM card and if you see signal bars. Let me know what you see, and if you can send picture messages. If the SIM is still not detected, I’ll help you with the next steps.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: poor
Cellular Network Type: 2G
Mobile Data Enabled: No
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No

Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in. Now my phone shows one bar for signal and says "2G," but it still says data is disabled. I haven’t tried sending a picture message yet. What should I do next?

Great job reseating the SIM card! Now that your phone detects the SIM and shows a signal, let’s address the next issues:

1. Your phone is currently connected to a 2G network, which is not suitable for sending MMS (picture messages).
2. Mobile data is still disabled, which is required for MMS.

Let’s do the following steps:
- First, enable mobile data on your phone. You can usually do this by swiping down from the top of your screen and tapping the mobile data icon to turn it on.
- Next, change your network mode to prefer 4G or 5G (if available) for better connectivity.

Please enable mobile data and let me know if you see a 4G, LTE, or 5G icon appear. If you need help changing your network mode, let me know your phone model, and I’ll guide you through it. Once mobile data is enabled and you’re on a 4G/5G network, try sending a picture message again and let me know the result.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Network Mode Preference: 2g_only

I turned on mobile data, but my phone still says "2G" and only shows one bar for signal. I checked, and it looks like my phone is set to use only 2G. How do I change it to 4G or something better? I’m not sure where to find that setting.

No problem! To improve your connection and enable MMS, you’ll need to change your network mode preference from 2G to 4G or 5G. Here’s how you can usually do this:

1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Select “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
4. Look for “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
5. Change the setting to “4G/5G preferred” or “LTE/4G/5G auto.”

If you don’t see these exact options, let me know your phone’s make and model, and I’ll provide step-by-step instructions specific to your device.

Once you’ve changed the network mode, check if your phone now shows “4G,” “LTE,” or “5G” in the status bar. Let me know when you’ve done this and if your signal improves. Then, try sending a picture message again.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I changed the network mode like you said, and now my phone shows excellent signal and says "5G" with data enabled. But I still can’t send picture messages—it's still not working. Is there something else I should try? This is getting a bit frustrating.

Thank you for your patience and for following the steps so far. Since your phone now has excellent signal, is on 5G, and data is enabled, but MMS still isn’t working, the next most common cause is incorrect APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for MMS.

Let’s check your APN settings:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Select “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
4. Tap on “Access Point Names” or “APN.”

Check if there is an APN set, and if there is an MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL listed. If you’re not sure what you’re seeing, let me know.

If the APN or MMSC settings look missing or incorrect, you should reset your APN settings to default. Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." I’m not sure if that’s right or not. Should I still try resetting these settings, or is there something else I should do?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. The APN name and MMSC URL you provided look generally correct, but sometimes resetting the APN settings to default can resolve hidden configuration issues that may not be obvious.

Let’s proceed with resetting your APN settings to default:
1. In the APN settings menu, look for an option like “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.”
2. Tap that option to reset your APN settings.

After resetting, you must reboot your phone for the changes to take effect.

Please reset your APN settings, then restart your phone. Once your phone is back on, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still have trouble sending MMS.

APN settings will reset at reboot.

I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else I can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I ever be able to send photos again?

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. I understand this is frustrating, but we still have a few more things we can check before escalating the issue.

Let’s check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled, as it can sometimes interfere with MMS. Please do the following:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Look for “Wi-Fi Calling.”
4. If Wi-Fi Calling is ON, please turn it OFF.

After turning off Wi-Fi Calling, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if Wi-Fi Calling was enabled and if turning it off helps. If MMS still doesn’t work, I’ll guide you through the next troubleshooting step.

Thank you for your patience and for trying all the troubleshooting steps so far. Since you’ve:
- Checked your signal and network mode,
- Enabled mobile data,
- Reset APN settings and rebooted,
- Turned off Wi-Fi Calling,

and MMS is still not working, we’ve covered all the standard troubleshooting steps available.
